questions.question: Define food irradiation and explain why it is referred to as cold sterilization.
questions.solution_html:
• Food irradiation is the treatment of food using ionizing radiation such as gamma rays, X
  • rays, or electron beams to destroy microorganisms and insects.
  • Why called cold sterilization
  • • It destroys microbes without raising food temperature significantly
  • • Nutritional quality is largely preserved
  • • Suitable for heat-sensitive foods
  • Uses: Extends shelf life, Prevents sprouting, Controls insects
questions.final_answer: Uses: Extends shelf life, Prevents sprouting, Controls insects
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the paired comparison test.
questions.solution_html:
• Paired comparison test is a sensory evaluation method in which two samples are
  • presented together and the judge compares them for a specific characteristic.
  • Procedure
  • • Two coded samples are given
  • • Judge compares for sweetness, saltiness, texture, etc.
  • • Judge selects sample with stronger characteristic
questions.final_answer: • Judge selects sample with stronger characteristic
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the process of emulsion formation.
questions.solution_html:
• Emulsion is a mixture of two immiscible liquids where one liquid is dispersed in another.
  • Process of emulsion formation
  • • Two liquids (oil and water) are mixed
  • • Mechanical agitation breaks one liquid into droplets
  • • Emulsifier stabilizes droplets
  • Types
  • • Oil in water (milk)
  • • Water in oil (butter)
questions.final_answer: • Water in oil (butter)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define Modified Atmosphere Packaging.
questions.solution_html:
• Modified Atmosphere Packaging (MAP) is a packaging technique in which the normal
  • air inside the package is replaced with a controlled gas mixture.
  • Common gases used: Oxygen, Carbon dioxide, Nitrogen
  • Advantages
  • • Extends shelf life
  • • Reduces microbial growth
  • • Maintains freshness
questions.final_answer: • Maintains freshness
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define food preservation and explain its objectives, importance, and need in modern society.
questions.solution_html:
• Food preservation is the process of preventing food spoilage and extending shelf life by
  • controlling microorganisms, enzymes, and chemical changes.
  • Objectives
  • • Prevent microbial spoilage
  • • Maintain nutritional quality
  • • Extend shelf life
  • • Ensure safety
  • Importance
  • • Reduces food wastage
  • • Makes seasonal foods available year-round
  • • Facilitates transport and storage
  • • Improves food security
  • Need in modern society
  • • Urbanization increases demand for stored foods
  • • Long-distance food transport
  • • Emergency food supply
  • • Convenience foods for busy lifestyles
  • Methods
  • • High temperature preservation
  • • Low temperature preservation
  • • Dehydration
  • • Irradiation
  • • Preservatives
questions.final_answer: • Preservatives
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
